           JOINT MOTION FOR LEAVE TO FILE DIRECT TESTIMONY
                      AND EXHIBITS OUT OF TIME


TO THE HONORABLE CASSANDRA QUINN DEE AND MARLO CHICO,
ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:

      1.      Pursuant to SOAH Order No. 6, the Intervenors listed below (collectively,

“Intervenors”), by and through undersigned counsel, jointly ﬁle this Response SeUing

Forth Good Cause for the late ﬁling of their Direct Testimony and request a hearing on

this issue, and in support thereof would show as follows:



                                           1
                                 I.     BACKGROUND

      2.      This proceeding involves the Joint Application of Oncor Electric Delivery

Company LLC and LCRA Transmission Services Corporation to Amend their Certiﬁcates

of Convenience and Necessity for the Bell County East Switch to Big Hill Substation 765-

kV Transmission Line in Bell, Burnet, Concho, Coryell, Lampasas, Llano, Mason,

McCulloch, Menard, Milam, Mills, San Saba, Schleicher, Tom Green, and Williamson

Counties. The Hearing on the Merits is scheduled for June 8–12, 2026.

      3.     On April 20, 2026, the Administrative Law Judges entered SOAH Order No.

6 establishing a procedural schedule in this proceeding and seUing May 13, 2026, as the

deadline for Intervenors to ﬁle direct testimony or statements of position.

      4.     Intervenors received notice regarding the proposed transmission line and

this proceeding only approximately thirty (30) days prior to the testimony deadline.

      5.     Due to the compressed timeline and diﬃculty securing representation in

this maUer, Intervenors retained undersigned counsel only shortly before the testimony

deadline.

      6.     Immediately upon being retained, undersigned counsel began preparing

testimony and exhibits, including conducting client meetings, gathering supporting

materials, and coordinating the preparation of expert testimony and exhibits.




                                            2
       7.     Counsel was required to prepare and organize a substantial volume of

intervenor testimony, exhibits, maps, photographs, and expert materials within a

compressed timeframe.

      8.     Counsel understood the ﬁling deadline to extend until midnight, consistent

with electronic ﬁling deadlines under the Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 6(a)(4)(A).

SOAH Order No. 6 does not expressly state that the ﬁling deadline was 5:00 p.m.

      9.     Undersigned counsel represents a large number of Intervenors in this

proceeding. On May 13, 2026, counsel undertook to ﬁle the direct testimony and exhibits

for all Intervenors on the same day as the deadline set in SOAH Order No. 6. Due to the

substantial volume of simultaneous ﬁlings required across multiple clients, combined

with the time required for the PUC Interchange System to separately process, conﬁrm,

and generate receipts for each individual ﬁling before subsequent ﬁlings could be

completed, several ﬁlings were not accepted by the Interchange system prior to 5:00 p.m.

      10.    Counsel and staﬀ worked diligently to ﬁnalize and upload the ﬁlings prior

to the deadline but encountered technical diﬃculties while processing and uploading the

unusually large volume of materials, including ﬁle synchronization issues, PDF issues,

and computer slowdowns.

      11.    The delay in ﬁling was not the result of intentional disregard, conscious

indiﬀerence, or lack of diligence. Rather, it resulted from these persons only recently

obtaining representation, the compressed procedural schedule, the substantial volume of



                                           3
 materials requiring preparation and technical diﬃculties encountered while completing

the ﬁlings.

       12.    The following Intervenors had Direct Testimony prepared and submiUed

for ﬁling on May 13, 2026, but the ﬁlings were not completed and accepted by the

Interchange system prior to the 5:00 p.m. deadline:

              a.   Dennis Cabaniss — 5:02 p.m.

              b.   Boyce Cabaniss — 5:10 p.m.

              c.   Debby Peterson — 5:11 p.m.

              d.   Michael Schulte — 5:51 p.m.

              e.   Kellianne Jenkins — 5:27 p.m.

              f.   Steven Keith Pate — 5:07 p.m.

              g.   BreU Stewart — 8:27 p.m.

              h.   John Barry Winder — 6:02 p.m.

              i.   Raul Gonzales — 5:04 p.m.

              j.   Jill DeVilleneuve — 5:55 p.m.

              k.   Donald Schaek — 6:15 p.m.

              l.   Misty Hoenig — 5:02 p.m.

              m.   Crystal Hutchinson — 5:28 p.m.

              n.   Lisa Lima — 5:48 p.m.

              o.   Linda Nail — 6:07 p.m.



                                            4
                 p.   Paige Gist — 6:00 p.m.

                q.   Kyle McFather — 5:23 p.m.

                r.   Joshua Shaver — 6:11 p.m.

                s.   Victoria Herndon — 6:04 p.m.

                t.   Michael Gier — 5:18 p.m.

                u.   Michelle Dawn King — 5:53 p.m.

                v.   Dustin King — 9:35 p.m.

       13.      Each Intervenor’s Direct Testimony was ﬁled on May 13, 2026, in opposition

to the proposed transmission line segments identiﬁed in their respective testimony.

                               II.    GOOD CAUSE EXISTS

       14.       Under 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 22.225, the presiding oﬃcers may admit late-

ﬁled evidence upon a showing of good cause, including where necessary to ensure full

disclosure of the facts.

       15.      Good cause exists here because:

             a. Intervenors received notice only approximately thirty days before the

                testimony deadline;

             b. Intervenors retained counsel shortly before the ﬁling deadline;

             c. Counsel diligently worked to prepare a substantial volume of intervenor

                and expert testimony and exhibits within a compressed timeframe;




                                               5
              d. SOAH Order No. 6 did not expressly state that the ﬁling deadline was 5:00

                p.m., and counsel reasonably understood the deadline to extend until

                midnight; and

             e. Counsel encountered technical diﬃculties while ﬁnalizing and uploading

                the ﬁlings.

       16.      Administrative Law Judges in similar transmission line proceedings have

granted leave for modestly late-ﬁled testimony and exhibits where delays resulted from

ﬁling misunderstandings, technical diﬃculties, or logistical issues associated with ﬁling

large volumes of testimony and exhibits.1

       17.      Texas courts have long recognized that relief from procedural default is

appropriate where a party’s failure to comply results from accident or mistake rather than

intentional or consciously indiﬀerent conduct, the party has a meritorious position, and

granting relief will not cause delay or undue prejudice. See Anderson v. R.R. Comm’n of

Tex., 963 S.W.2d 217, 219–20 (Tex. App.—Austin 1998, no pet.). Here, the late ﬁlings

resulted from compressed deadlines, and technical and logistical diﬃculties—not

conscious indiﬀerence—and granting leave will not prejudice any party or disrupt the

procedural schedule.




1See, e.g., SOAH Order No. 10, PUC Docket No. 59336 (granting leave for late-ﬁled testimony and exhibits
based on ﬁling diﬃculties and related circumstances).


                                                   6
        18.    Allowing the testimony and exhibits to be ﬁled will ensure a complete and

fully developed record regarding the routing and impacts of the proposed transmission

line on aﬀected landowners and properties.

                            III.   NO UNDUE PREJUDICE

       19.    Granting this Motion will not unduly prejudice any party.

       20.    The delay in ﬁling was minimal and occurred suﬃciently in advance of the

hearing on the merits to allow all parties adequate time to review the testimony and

exhibits, conduct discovery, prepare objections, and prepare for cross-examination.

       21.    Acceptance of these testimonies will not prejudice any party. The deadline

for objections to Intervenor direct testimony is May 18, 2026, and the Hearing on the

Merits is not scheduled until June 8–12, 2026, leaving all parties ample time to review and

respond to Intervenors’ testimony. Denial of this Motion, however, would substantially

prejudice Intervenors by preventing consideration of testimony and evidence regarding

the impacts of the proposed transmission line on aﬀected landowners and properties and

would unnecessarily limit the development of a full and complete evidentiary record.

       22.    Intervenors do not object to the current procedural schedule and intend to

comply with all deadlines going forward. Intervenors will also cooperate with any

reasonable requests regarding review of or response to the late-ﬁled testimony and

exhibits.




                                             7
        23.    Allowing the late-ﬁled testimony and exhibits will promote the fair and

complete development of the record, which is particularly important in a transmission

line proceeding involving substantial impacts to private property rights.


                     IV.    REQUEST FOR HEARING AND PRAYER

       24.    WHEREFORE, PREMISES CONSIDERED, and pursuant to SOAH Order

No. 6, the above-listed Intervenors respectfully request that the Administrative Law

Judges: (1) ﬁnd that good cause exists for the late ﬁling of their Direct Testimony; (2) set

a hearing on this issue as contemplated by SOAH Order No. 6; (3) accept for ﬁling the

Direct Testimony of each Intervenor listed above, all ﬁled on May 13, 2026; and (4) grant

such other and further relief to which Intervenors may be justly entitled.


                                                 Respectfully submitted,

                                                 GRISSOM & THOMPSON, L.L.P
